overview: Direct support professionals are workers who help people with intellectual and developmental disabilities live independently, assisting with daily tasks, jobs, errands, and community life. The federal government sorts jobs into categories under the Standard Occupational Classification system, which statistical agencies use to collect data on employment and wages, and these workers currently have no category of their own. This bill directs the White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB), which oversees that system, to consider creating a separate code for direct support professionals as a healthcare support job in its next revision. If OMB decides not to, it must explain why to Congress within one month. The bill provides no new funding. As of September 14, 2026, it had been approved by a Senate committee and placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say these workers do different work than home health or personal care aides, and a separate job code would give officials accurate data on high turnover and staff shortages that affect people with disabilities.
against: Critics say the bill only asks OMB to consider a change, so its effect may be limited, and job classification decisions are best left to the statistical experts who review the system.
